title: Adaptive KV trimming + progressive batching with model-swap fallback to prevent OOMs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Intermittent OOMs on high-concurrency inference nodes when large KV caches coincide with wide continuous batches. Existing hard-eviction + global admission throttles are brittle for latency-sensitive customers. Goal: implement a nuanced runtime strategy that trims KV usage adaptively, reduces batch memory footprint progressively, and supports an automated model-swap fallback to smaller quantized variants with transparent retry so requests succeed instead of failing. This ticket scopes the design, implementation spikes, unit+integration tests, and gradual rollout for production clusters.
updates: 2026-02-19 - Spike: profiled OOM incidents across 3 clusters. Found pattern: cold-starts + long-context chat sessions push KV and batch amplification. Memory pressure correlates with tail latency bursts and KV hit-rate drop.

2026-02-22 - Design doc drafted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Adaptive+KV+Trimming (internal). Core primitives: KV half-life, progressive batch width reduction, per-request KV-reservation tags, and model-swap API handshake.

2026-02-25 - Spike-2: implemented KV half-life simulator in local runtime; tuning suggests decay window ~120s for chat workloads reduces steady-state KV by ~22% without losing >2% exact-match cache hits.

2026-03-01 - Proposal review with Runtime and Infra: accepted progressive batching thresholds (90th/95th latency bands), slot-based KV quotas per model, and model-swap policy configs. Trade-off noted: more aggressive trimming reduces cost but increases cold-token recomputation.
2026-03-04 - Implemented core: kv_trim controller, batch_admission shim, and model_swap orchestrator. Added metrics: kv_trim_count, batch_reduction_events, model_swap_invocations, swap_success_rate.

2026-03-08 - End-to-end test harness: synthetic workload with mixed long-context chats. System completed degraded path: trimmed KV -> reduced batch width -> triggered model-swap to 8-bit micro-model -> request succeeded with slightly higher latency. Recorded no OOMs in 10k trial requests.

2026-03-10 - Code review (PR #4128): feedback from infra to add backpressure signals and a safer default config. Addressing comments: add per-route opt-out and observability labels for swapped requests.
Next steps: finalize config defaults, run staged canary on canary-rt-2 cluster (10% traffic), update runbooks and expose rollback toggles in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime avoids OOMs on previously failing workload (reproduce testbed) for 48h under production-like concurrency
Model-swap path succeeds >= 99% of the time when triggered, with clear telemetry tagging swapped requests
No customer-facing 5xx errors attributable to OOMs during canary (10% traffic) for 7 days
Config knobs (kv_half_life, batch_width_shrink_ratio, swap_thresholds) present and documented
Performance regression < 10% p95 latency increase for non-swapped traffic
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - internal test harness + integration tests (complete)
Stage 1 - small canary (canary-rt-2): 10% of traffic, enable graceful defaults, monitor OOMs & swap metrics for 72h
Stage 2 - regional ramp to 50% after 72h stable metrics, enable auto-swap for high-impact models only
Stage 3 - global rollout with release 1.22, expose console toggles and alerting for swap events
Rollback: disable model-swap and revert kv_trim to conservative defaults via remote flags; documented in runbook RB-20678
related_links: Incident postmortem that motivated this work: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/2026-01-13-oom-chat-cluster
notes: Design decisions: prefer soft trimming (LRU-adjacent TTL heuristics and partial KV eviction per-conversation) over global hard dumps to minimize user-visible context loss.
Fallback model candidates: prioritized by quantization level and architecture compatibility; prefer 8-bit causal variants with matching tokenizer to avoid output drift.
Observability: tag swapped requests with header X-RWD-Model-Swapped and include swap_reason in traces; surface aggregated metric `swap_latency_regression` in Console.
SLA considerations: document potential quality regressions for customers on Dedicated plans; require opt-in for auto-swap outside hosted tier.
Trade-offs: aggressive trimming reduces OOM risk but may increase token re-generation leading to higher per-request compute cost; treat cost vs reliability as a configurable policy per-customer.
Open question: exact default kv_half_life value. Current experiments use 120s; require more traffic variety to finalize.
